notes: Authentication is delayed: signing and verification never delay original surveillance transmission, and no authentication-age deadline discards work.
The experiment follows each observed trace for 60 additional seconds. Unfinished work remains pending and is reported as censored at the horizon.
Coverage thresholds describe elapsed authentication delay; they do not impose expiration or admission policy.
Queue capacities are explicitly unbounded in these scenarios; the finite input trace and follow-up horizon bound observation, not queue memory.
The 100 additional authentication frames per second per aircraft is a hypothetical configured budget, not a regulatory allowance.
Independent and destructive-overlap channel cases use the same one-percent IID exogenous loss assumption and seed. No extra background traffic is added.
Destructive overlap is a simplified collision sensitivity model; it does not model receiver capture effects, interference power or unseen traffic.
One development seed does not establish confidence intervals.

scenarios.name: fixed_k_independent
scenarios.description: Fixed-count grouping; incomplete final tails remain unsigned. Independent reception loss without collision erasure. Continue authentication without expiry through a finite follow-up horizon.

scenarios.name: fixed_k_collision
scenarios.description: Fixed-count grouping; incomplete final tails remain unsigned. Any overlap among modeled channel frames destroys the overlapping receptions. Continue authentication without expiry through a finite follow-up horizon.

scenarios.name: bounded_batch_independent
scenarios.description: Close a group at k messages or one second. Independent reception loss without collision erasure. Continue authentication without expiry through a finite follow-up horizon.

scenarios.name: bounded_batch_collision
scenarios.description: Close a group at k messages or one second. Any overlap among modeled channel frames destroys the overlapping receptions. Continue authentication without expiry through a finite follow-up horizon.
